name: Oetz
kurzbeschreibung: The gateway to the Ötztal, featuring the famous Stuibenfall, Tirol’s longest suspension bridge, and the outdoor adventure center.
text:
Overview

Oetz is situated at the sunny entrance to the Ötztal Valley in the Tyrolean district of Imst, about 50 kilometres southwest of Innsbruck at an elevation of 820 metres. This heritage-rich tourism municipality has around 2,400 residents and spans 29.2 square kilometres, extending from the banks of the roaring Ötztaler Ache river across rolling meadow terraces up to the jagged peak of Mount Acherkogel (3,007 m) – the northernmost three-thousander of the Stubai Alps. Thanks to its sheltered valley basin location, Oetz enjoys an exceptionally mild microclimate. The historic village centre captivates visitors with elaborately frescoed merchant houses and historic inns reflecting centuries of alpine hospitality. As the primary hub of the front Ötztal, Oetz perfectly combines natural lakeside relaxation at Tyrol's warmest mountain lake with immediate access to the high-alpine skiing and hiking terrain of Hochoetz.

History

Settlement in the lower Ötztal dates back to the Neolithic era and Roman times. The village was first documented between 1166 and 1170 under the name Ez. Oetz developed early on into the economic and judicial centre of the valley, favoured by packhorse trade across the Timmelsjoch pass into South Tyrol. An outstanding architectural monument is the Turmmuseum Oetz: this medieval residential tower dating from around 1350 is the oldest secular stone building in the Ötztal and now houses an internationally acclaimed collection of alpine landscape painting and sacred art. The village scape is adorned with intricate Renaissance facade paintings, notably on the Gasthof zum Stern dating back to the 16th century. Perched majestically on a rock outcrop above the village is the late Gothic Parish Church of Saints George and Nicholas, lavishly baroqueized in later centuries.

Getting There

Reaching Oetz is remarkably fast and easy due to its location at the entrance to the valley. By car, leave the Inntal Autobahn A12 at the Ötztal exit and follow the well-engineered Ötztal federal road B186 for just six kilometres directly into the town centre, with driving time from Innsbruck taking around 40 minutes. Rail travellers arrive at the Ötztal Bahnhof station on the Arlberg Railway line, which is served regularly by international Railjet and Intercity express trains. Directly outside the station building, modern VVT regional bus route 320 runs at frequent 30-minute intervals, reaching Oetz in less than ten minutes. Cyclists can also reach the village along the scenic Ötztal Cycle Path leading from the Inn Valley up into the valley.

Tips

The crown jewel of nature here is Lake Piburg (Piburger See), idyllically nestled in a dense pine forest above Oetz at 913 metres: designated as a protected natural monument, with summer water temperatures reaching up to 24 to 25 degrees Celsius, it is celebrated as the warmest natural swimming lake in Tyrol, reflecting the pyramidal peak of Mount Acherkogel. In winter, the Hochoetz ski area beckons families and skiers: the Acherkogelbahn cable car whisks guests straight from the village to 39 kilometres of snow-sure ski runs and the WIDIVERSUM mountain adventure park at 2,000 metres. Whitewater kayakers worldwide know Oetz for the Wellerbrücke rapids on the Ötztaler Ache river, legendary site of the Sickline extreme kayak world championships. Art lovers should explore the Turmmuseum collections.
